title: World-review Phase 1: User-Facing Data Correctness Fixes
outcome: Implemented all 4 Phase 1 bug fixes (WR-1 through WR-4) using TDD. All 61 tests pass (14 new + 47 existing) with zero regressions.
key_decisions: WR-1: Added project_name parameter to merge_datasets() with default '' for backward compatibility, rather than modifying generate_report.py post-merge. This follows DIP — the caller injects the dependency.
WR-2: Used token-ratio approximation (sessions * build_tok / total_effective) to estimate build sessions per commit date, with max(1, ...) floor and min() clamp as safety net.

WR-3: Added total_per_model and reasoning_tokens to cost_summary, and total_per_model to cache_cost_summary. Updated HTML renderer to use per-model pricing as primary display, consolidating two cost tiers into one canonical figure.
WR-4: Set build_prod['date'] = 'all' to communicate this is a cross-date aggregate, per plan convention.
learnings: The existing test suite uses class-based pytest organization with spec references in docstrings (e.g., '1.2.1.1'). Followed the same convention for new tests.
merge_datasets() is the central assembly function — all Phase 1 fixes converged on it, confirming it as the right place for data corrections.
The productive_build_sessions bug (8 > 5) was caught cleanly by a test comparing against total_build_sessions, demonstrating effective example-first testing.
Cost card HTML rendering needed updating alongside data changes to ensure consistency between JSON output and HTML display.
next_steps: Phase 2 (WR-5): Add documentation comment to _resolve_date() truthiness pattern in queries/utils.py — low priority, current behavior is correct
Run generate_report.py against a real project to verify HTML output renders correctly with per-model cost cards
Verify meta.title in generated JSON contains actual project name, not placeholder
